title: Localized relation membership and Jacobian left inverse from a conormal basis
statement: Let $R,A$ be commutative rings and let $P:R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a finite $R$-algebra presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] with relations $f_0,\ldots,f_{m-1}$ and kernel $I=(f_j)$. Let $a\in A$, let $h=P.\sigma(a)$ be the chosen polynomial lift of $a$, and put $B=A_a$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Assume $B$ smooth over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], $c\leq\min(n,m)$, and a $B$-basis $b_0,\ldots,b_{c-1}$ of $B\otimes_A I/I^2$ with $b_j=1\otimes(f_j\bmod I^2)$. Put $K=(f_0,\ldots,f_{c-1})+I^2$ in the polynomial ring and $D_{ij}=\overline{\partial f_j/\partial x_i}$ in $A$ [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]. Then every $f_j$ for $j\geq c$ maps into the extension of $K$ in $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]_h$, and there is a $c\times n$ matrix $L$ over $B$ with $L D_B=1_c$, where $D_B$ is the image of $D$ under $A\to B$.

proof.text: The basis expresses each remaining relation class in the localized conormal module as sum of coefficients times the initial classes. Write the finitely many coefficients as fractions of A elements with powers of a as denominators; lift their numerators to the polynomial ring. Clear a common denominator. Equality in the localization gives another power annihilating the difference in I/I^2. Multiplication by h on I/I^2 is multiplication by a. Hence h^N f_j is in the initial-relation ideal plus I^2. Since h is invertible in the polynomial localization, f_j belongs to the extension of that ideal.

Transport the smooth localized conormal differential and its left inverse from the polynomial quotient to A using P.quotientEquiv. Identify the middle term with B^n on the coordinate differentials and the source with B^c through b. The image of b_j has ith coordinate the image in B of the evaluated partial derivative of f_j. Compose the left inverse with b.equivFun and write it in coordinate bases. This gives L with L D_B=1_c. If c=0 all matrices have zero columns/rows and the identity is the empty one; the zero localization is also allowed.

theorem localized_conormal_basis_jacobian
    {R : Type u} {A : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    {n m c : ℕ} (P : Presentation R A (Fin n) (Fin m))
    (hc : c ≤ min n m) (a : A) [Smooth R (Localization.Away a)]
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin c) (Localization.Away a)
      (Localization.Away a ⊗[A] P.toExtension.Cotangent))
    (hb : ∀ j : Fin c, b j = 1 ⊗ₜ[A]
      (Extension.Cotangent.mk (P := P.toExtension)
        ⟨P.relation (Fin.castLE (le_trans hc (min_le_right n m)) j),
          P.relation_mem_ker _⟩)) :
    (∀ j : Fin m, c ≤ j.val →
      algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (Localization.Away (P.σ a)) (P.relation j) ∈
        Ideal.map (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (Localization.Away (P.σ a)))
          (Ideal.span {f | ∃ k : Fin m, k.val < c ∧ f = P.relation k} +
            (Ideal.span (Set.range P.relation)) ^ 2)) ∧
    let D : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin c) (Localization.Away a) :=
      fun i j ↦ algebraMap A (Localization.Away a)
        (MvPolynomial.aeval P.val (MvPolynomial.pderiv i
          (P.relation (Fin.castLE (le_trans hc (min_le_right n m)) j))))
    ∃ L : Matrix (Fin c) (Fin n) (Localization.Away a), L * D = 1
